body.target_estimand: \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)=(V,\bigcup_{\ell\in[K]}E(\mathcal G_\ell))\), identified exactly as an oriented union
body.estimand_functional: \(\bigl(\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(\varnothing),\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(I_1),\ldots,\mathcal O_{\mathbf G}(I_N)\bigr)\mapsto\mathsf T(\mathbf G),\quad N=N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\)

sampling_model.design: Adaptive population-oracle design: \(I_j\subseteq V\), \(|I_j|\le s\), is measurable with respect to the preceding complete-oracle transcript; \(I=\varnothing\) is free.
sampling_model.units: On the standard Borel product space \(\mathcal X_V\), component \(\ell\) has DAG \(\mathcal G_\ell\), kernels \(\kappa_{\ell i}\), and law \(P_\ell(dx_V)=\prod_{i\in V}\kappa_{\ell i}(dx_i\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_\ell(i)})\); the latent component has weights \(\mathbf w\).
sampling_model.treatment: A stochastic hard intervention on \(I\) uses the same kernel \(q_i\) for vertex \(i\) across every component and every target containing \(i\), inducing \(P_{\ell,I}=\prod_{i\in I}q_i\prod_{i\notin I}\kappa_{\ell i}\) and deleting every component and selector edge entering copies of \(I\).
sampling_model.overlap: All mixture weights are strictly positive; no finite-sample conditional-independence margin is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None at this stage: \(P_I=\sum_{\ell\in L}w_\ell P_{\ell,I}\), \(\Delta\) is exactly the set of vertices whose lifted observational kernels vary across components, and simultaneous I-mixture faithfulness identifies each complete conditional-independence oracle with barred-copy d-separation in \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The proposed algorithm uses a total of \(\mathcal O(n^2)\) interventions.
For any mixture, an intervention of size at most \(|\operatorname{pa}_{\mathrm m}(i)|+1\) identifies a queried mixture-parent relation.
For some ground-truth ordering, every deterministic adaptive algorithm on a complete skeleton designs a separating system.
A verifying set separates every covered edge that remains unoriented in the observational essential graph.
There is an \(r\)-adaptive single-DAG algorithm with approximation \(\mathcal O(\min\{r,\log n\}n^{1/\min\{r,\log n\}})\) to verification.
With infinite interventional data, the central-node tree algorithm uses at most twice the minimum achievable number of interventions.
Each single-DAG interventional Markov equivalence class has a unique interventional essential-graph representative.
The mixture-DAG representation satisfies a global Markov property for the observational mixture distribution.
Ranks of aggregated moment matrices reveal a shared causal graph when the latent class count is small relative to graph size and sparsity.

body.tldr: The paper characterizes the experiment-count cost of recovering the oriented union of a latent mixture of DAGs when each intervention can target at most \(s\) variables. The formal kernel is an explicit universal-factor frontier for \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\), paired with the exact finite-versus-infinite size threshold, legal full-oracle transcript adversaries, and exact count formulas for directed-tree mixtures and cycle-free mixture ancestry. The upper construction batches emergent-path parent blockers; the lower construction packs alternatives that coexist on one I-mixture-faithful baseline transcript.

project_justification.gap: Varıcı et al. identify worst-case local intervention sizes and give a quadratic-count algorithm, but explicitly leave bounded-size intervention-count lower bounds open. Single-DAG count arguments condition on a known skeleton or essential graph and therefore do not control emergent nonedges or selector-induced ancestor cycles.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a five-parameter minimax resource law for complete I-mixture conditional-independence oracles, including a legal notion of which blocker requirements can coexist against adaptation.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a descendant-signature representation of the hard oracle subclass, proves the exact feasibility boundary, builds an explicit parent-blocking cover, and resolves the remaining gap through a legal blocker-packing benchmark that yields matching universal-factor bounds and exact structured-class formulas.

body.related_work: Varıcı et al. (2024) supply the component factorization, shared stochastic hard interventions, I-mixture faithfulness, local \(\Delta\)-through-path blocker tests, and CADIM; their Conclusion names constrained-size count lower bounds as open. Shanmugam et al. (2015) show that adaptive discovery on a complete single-DAG skeleton can be forced to realize a separating system, but their total-order transcript does not establish a legal mixture lower pair. Choo, Shiragur, and Bhattacharyya (2022) characterize single-DAG verification by covered-edge separation and compare adaptive search to that benchmark; the present work is informed by their charging idea but replaces covered reversals by true-edge-versus-emergent alternatives. Choo and Shiragur (2023) study round-limited adaptivity for one DAG, not heterogeneous mixture-union identification. Greenewald et al. (2019) motivate a centroid potential for one known causal tree, whereas the tree-mixture result must track \(K\) componentwise paths and a non-tree union. Saeed, Panigrahi, and Uhler (2020) establish observational mixture-DAG Markov semantics under a more restrictive recovery regime. Hauser and Bühlmann (2012) provide the single-DAG equivalence archetype but are not a claimed target of the count theorem. Mazaheri et al. (2026) observe aggregated moment matrices and use their ranks to recover graphical properties of one shared underlying DAG across latent populations. Their observational moment-rank information and shared-graph target are non-nested with the present adaptive interventional-CI oracle and heterogeneous oriented-union target, so their theorem is not a comparator count bound.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing all-parameter step remains coexistence of blocker requirements on one legal baseline transcript. The verified finite evidence is not itself a theorem: exhaustive evaluation covered all \(543\) four-node DAGs paired into \(63{,}432\) union-indegree-at-most-two mixtures and all \(24{,}357{,}888\) barred-copy conditional-separation queries, with no discrepancy from the descendant-signature rule; twelve positive rational fixtures also passed \(6{,}272\) exact probability conditional-independence checks. Uniform faithful realization and the general packing rate remain formal obligations.
body.honest_scope: The exact feasibility boundary, the size-\(d\) cycle-free policy, full-oracle reduction, explicit parent-blocking upper design, legal transcript lemma, three exact slices, universal-factor frontier, and two structured exact formulas are all posed as results to prove over the completed shared-kernel model. The proposal does not claim finite-sample conditional-independence recovery from faithfulness alone. The classical boundary \(K=1\) is outside the displayed new parameter class and reduces to single-DAG bounded-intervention design; \(d=0\) reduces to the known empty union, and \(s=n-1\) admits the complement-singleton dense reduction.
